headline: Data Engineer Salary 2026 USA: What You Can Earn
metaDescription: Data engineer salary 2026 USA: average base $125K-$135K, entry $80K-$105K, senior $147K-$179K+, San Francisco pay and the skills that raise your salary.

sections.content:
In 2026, the average base salary for a data engineer in the United States is about $125,000 to $135,000. Glassdoor reports an average near $132,000, ZipRecruiter lists about $129,716, and Indeed reports around $136,000. The median base salary is about $131,000, and median total compensation, including bonuses and equity, is roughly $155,000.

Pay varies widely by experience, location and employer. Entry-level engineers start far below the average, while senior engineers at large technology companies can earn total compensation of $200,000 to $250,000 or more. The demand for engineers who build reliable data pipelines remains strong as companies invest in AI and analytics.
sections.title: How much does a data engineer earn in 2026?

sections.content:
Entry-level data engineers typically earn $80,000 to $105,000 in base salary. At this stage, employers look for solid SQL and Python skills, basic cloud knowledge and an understanding of data modelling. Internships and personal projects with real pipelines help new graduates reach the upper end of this range.

Mid-level engineers earn about $119,000 to $150,000, while senior engineers earn $147,000 to $179,000 or more in base pay. Senior roles add architecture, mentoring and ownership of critical pipelines. At big technology companies, senior total compensation often reaches $200,000 to $250,000 once stock and bonuses are included.
sections.title: Salary by experience level

sections.content:
San Francisco pays the most, with an average data engineer salary of about $183,000. New York, Seattle and Boston also pay well above the national average, though the cost of living in these cities is high. Remote roles have narrowed some gaps, but location-based pay bands still exist at many companies.

Large technology companies generally offer the highest total compensation because stock grants add substantially to base pay. Startups may offer lower base salaries with equity that could grow in value. Regulated industries such as finance and healthcare often pay competitively for engineers who handle sensitive data securely.
sections.title: Location and company differences

sections.content:
The core skills are SQL, Python, cloud platforms and pipeline tools such as Spark and Airflow. Engineers who design scalable data warehouses, manage streaming data and automate data quality checks command higher pay. Experience with modern lakehouse platforms and orchestration tools is increasingly expected.

The most valuable engineers combine strong engineering with business understanding: they know which data matters, document their pipelines and deliver reliable data for AI and analytics teams. Open-source contributions, certifications and a track record of shipping production pipelines all strengthen salary negotiations more than any single credential.
